title: The call
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, small-town 911 dispatch center at night and snowy suburban streets on Christmas Eve, dim console glow, cold green and deep red tones, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 1. A 911 call on Christmas Eve from a house with no phone line. ☎️

Original fiction. Part 2 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Every dispatcher gets one call they never forget. June Calder got hers at 11:52 on Christmas Eve.
scenes.image: a woman with a headset sitting alone at a dispatch console at night, face lit by soft glow

scenes.narration: The dispatch center was quiet. Tinsel taped to the monitors. A plate of cookies nobody touched. Snow piling up against the only window.
scenes.image: a quiet dispatch room at night with tinsel on the consoles and snow piling against a window

scenes.narration: Line four lit up. 911, what's the address of your emergency?
scenes.image: close-up of a single glowing button on a dark dispatch phone console

scenes.narration: An old man's voice. Thin. Polite. Eighteen Larkspur Road.
scenes.image: a woman pressing her headset closer to her ear, frowning in concentration

scenes.narration: June knew that address. There was no phone line at Eighteen Larkspur Road. There never had been.
scenes.image: an old two-story house alone at the end of a snowy road at night, no lights on

scenes.narration: Sir, what's happening? He said: they're singing outside again.
scenes.image: snow falling past a dark window of an old house at night

scenes.narration: And she heard it. Behind his breathing. A dozen voices, singing an old carol in perfect harmony. Slow. Too slow.
scenes.image: faint silhouettes of a dozen carolers standing in falling snow in front of a dark house

scenes.narration: How many people, sir? Same as always, he said. Are you hurt? Not yet. They only come up to the porch on the last verse.
scenes.image: a snowy porch with a dried wreath on the door, shadows gathering at the steps

scenes.narration: June sent a patrol car. She stayed on the line. The singing got louder. Closer. The verses ticking down.
scenes.image: police car with lights glowing driving down a snowy residential street at night

scenes.narration: Then the old man whispered: here's the last verse. And the line went dead. But the singing kept going in her headset. On a line that wasn't connected anymore.
scenes.image: close-up of a woman's frozen face in console glow, headset on, eyes wide
